entry.title: Service Worker Capability Delegation for Pop-ups
entry.content:
WebKittens

@annevk @youennf @cdumez

Title of the proposal

Service Worker Capability Delegation for Pop-ups

URL to the spec

https://htmlpreview.github.io/?https://github.com/dmurph/capability-delegation/blob/popup-delegation-spec/spec.html

  • Spec Source & Diff (spec.bs): WICG/capability-delegation#44
  • Base WICG Specification: https://wicg.github.io/capability-delegation/spec.html

URL to the spec's repository

https://github.com/WICG/capability-delegation

Issue Tracker URL

No response

Explainer URL

https://github.com/WICG/capability-delegation/blob/main/explainers/popup-delegation.md

TAG Design Review URL

w3ctag/design-reviews#1295

Mozilla standards-positions issue URL

mozilla/standards-positions#1474

WebKit Bugzilla URL

No response

Radar URL

No response

Description

Summary

This proposal extends the Capability Delegation framework so that a Service Worker can delegate the "popup" capability to a same-origin WindowClient during a trusted notificationclick event (client.postMessage(message, {delegate: 'popup'})).

In the document-bound Notifications API (new Notification()), a user click dispatches an onclick event on a Window with transient user activation. That handler can call window.open() to open a popup window that shares memory with the main application tab. In Service Worker notifications (registration.showNotification()), the notificationclick event runs in the background worker without a DOM. Clients.openWindow() can only open a standalone top-level tab with no window.opener reference, which forces a full application reload.

With this proposal:

  1. A trusted notificationclick event grants a single-use "popup" capability token to the NotificationEvent context (5-second maximum lifetime).
  2. The Service Worker brings an open same-origin client tab to the foreground (await client.focus()) and calls client.postMessage(msg, {delegate: 'popup'}), which consumes the worker token.
  3. The target WindowClient receives a transient delegated "popup" capability timestamp (1-second lifetime).
  4. A synchronous window.open() call in the client window consumes both transient user activation (if present) and the delegated "popup" capability token. This preserves a strict 1:1 ratio between one user notification click and one opened popup window.

Related Links

  • W3C TAG Design Review: w3ctag/design-reviews#1295 (prior Capability Delegation review: w3ctag/design-reviews#655)
  • Prior WebKit Capability Delegation Position: #178
  • Prior Mozilla Capability Delegation Position: mozilla/standards-positions#565
  • Security & Privacy Self-Review Questionnaire: https://github.com/WICG/capability-delegation/blob/main/explainers/popup-delegation-security-privacy-questionnaire.md
  • Specification Diff (spec.bs): WICG/capability-delegation@main...dmurph:capability-delegation:popup-delegation-spec

entry.title: The focusreset event
entry.content:
WebKittens

@rniwa @annevk

Title of the proposal

The focusreset event

URL to the spec

whatwg/html#13050

URL to the spec's repository

https://github.com/whatwg/html

Issue Tracker URL

whatwg/html#12842

Explainer URL

https://github.com/noamr/explainers/blob/main/focusreset-explainer.md

TAG Design Review URL

No response

Mozilla standards-positions issue URL

mozilla/standards-positions#1469

WebKit Bugzilla URL

https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=327387

Radar URL

No response

Description

When the currently focused element in a document (or one of its ancestors) is removed from the DOM, the HTML Standard's node-remove focus fixup rule synchronously resets the document's focused area to its viewport (document.body / document.documentElement) without firing blur or focusout.

Because no event is fired when focus is lost due to DOM removal, UI component libraries, modal focus traps, and keyboard navigation tools currently rely on expensive or fragile workarounds such as attaching a MutationObserver({ childList: true, subtree: true }) to document.body (e.g., Radix UI's FocusScope, focus-trap) or polling document.activeElement via setInterval (e.g., Material UI's FocusTrap, Tridactyl).

This proposal introduces a focusreset event (and onfocusreset event handler IDL attribute) on Document. When a focused element is removed from a document that has focus—resetting focus to the viewport—a focus reset is signaled for that document. In the mutation observer microtask checkpoint (notify mutation observers, immediately after MutationObserver callbacks and slotchange events), if focus has not been explicitly moved to another element and the document still has focus, a focusreset event is fired at Document.

Specification PRs & Tests:

  • HTML PR: whatwg/html#13050
  • DOM PR: whatwg/dom#1512
  • WPT PR: web-platform-tests/wpt#63595

entry.title: SVG Path Data API: getPathData(), setPathData(), getPathSegmentAtLength()
entry.content:
WebKittens

@karlcow

Title of the proposal

SVG Paths-Mixin SVGPathData

URL to the spec

https://w3c.github.io/svgwg/specs/paths/#InterfaceSVGPathData

URL to the spec's repository

https://github.com/w3c/svgwg

Issue Tracker URL

https://github.com/w3c/svgwg/issues

Explainer URL

https://github.com/MicrosoftEdge/MSEdgeExplainers/blob/main/SVG/SVGPathDataAPI/explainer.md

TAG Design Review URL

w3ctag/design-reviews#1292

Mozilla standards-positions issue URL

https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1934525

WebKit Bugzilla URL

https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=328103

Radar URL

No response

Description

Adds structured JavaScript access to SVG path data through three methods on SVGPathElement: getPathData() reads the path as an array of {type, values} objects containing each segment's command and numeric parameters. setPathData() updates the path from such an array, getPathSegmentAtLength() returns the segment at a specified distance along the path. These methods let developers inspect, edit, and construct paths without manually parsing or serializing the d attribute.

The optional getPathData({normalize: true}) setting simplifies path data to absolute move, line, cubic Bézier, and close commands (M, L, C, and Z). All three APIs operate on the base value of the d attribute, not CSS-computed or animated values.

Without this feature, inspecting or modifying individual SVG path segments requires parsing and serializing the d attribute string, often using third-party libraries. This makes tasks such as path animation, hit-testing, and programmatic path construction unnecessarily complex and error-prone.

Implementing the SVG Working Group’s replacement API provides a simpler, standardized way to read and modify path segments without custom string parsing or polyfills.

Please let me know if you have any questions.

entry.title: Sealed form fields (`<sealedinput>` and the `sealed-fields` CSP directive)
entry.content:
WebKittens

No response

Title of the proposal

Sealed form fields (<sealedinput> and the sealed-fields CSP directive)

URL to the spec

WICG/proposals#307

URL to the spec's repository

https://github.com/madeit-build/koschei

Issue Tracker URL

No response

Explainer URL

https://github.com/madeit-build/koschei/blob/main/docs/specs/explainer.md

TAG Design Review URL

No response

Mozilla standards-positions issue URL

mozilla/standards-positions#1468

WebKit Bugzilla URL

No response

Radar URL

No response

Description

Today any script on a page can read a sensitive form value (card number, national ID, API key, medical answer) from the first keystroke, and the value is plaintext at every hop after TLS terminates: CDN, WAF, APM traces, logs.

This proposal adds a form control whose value is encrypted in the browser, via HPKE (RFC 9180), to a public key published by the form's action origin at /.well-known/sealed-input, before page script can observe it. .value returns the envelope, so FormData, constraint validation, and form libraries keep working. Envelopes are bound to the origin, action, and field name, so a ciphertext lifted from one site opens nowhere else. A companion CSP directive, sealed-fields cc-number cc-csc current-password, lets policy seal ordinary inputs by autocomplete token.

Threat model: defends against page script, third-party dependencies, extension content scripts, session replay, and TLS-terminating intermediaries. It does not defend against a compromised renderer, and it adds no party that wouldn't already hold the plaintext.

Precedent: Apple Pay JS has returned merchant-encrypted payment tokens to page script for a decade, and the Digital Credentials API returns HPKE-encrypted responses the page cannot read. This generalizes that shape to arbitrary fields.

Implementations: a polyfill (form-associated custom element sealing inside a recipient-served iframe) and a native implementation in Ladybird (13 patches with engine tests). One server opens envelopes from both. The native work surfaced plaintext channels that had to be closed (cloneNode, type switching, paste events, detach/reinsert, execCommand("undo") replaying edits against the validity bit, and editing history surviving a name or action change):
https://github.com/madeit-build/koschei/blob/main/docs/research/native-feasibility-ladybird.md

Where WebKit input would help most:

  1. Whether the hooks are shaped right for WebKit's text-input and editing architecture (autocorrect, dictation, AutoFill, undo).
  2. Whether the decoy-field answer in the explainer is sufficient, or whether the element shouldn't ship without the CSP directive.
  3. Open design questions: input event granularity (per-keystroke events leak length and cadence) and declared derived signals such as card brand.

WICG discussion: WICG/proposals#307

Description

Defines a reusable, parameterized block of style declarations and nested style rules with the @mixin rule, then expands them in place within a style rule via @apply as if the mixin's contents had been written there directly. The mixin body puts the declarations and rules to emit inside an @Result block, while any local custom properties used to compute them stay private and never reach the element; parameters can be typed and given defaults, and @Result can contain conditional rules such as @supports and @media. This lets authors package consistent patterns – component styles, effects like gradient text, responsive shorthands – once and reuse them across a stylesheet without a CSS pre-processor.

Description

The proposal changes radio-button activation so that activating the currently checked radio button can return an optional radio group to its no-selection state. If the group has a radio button with a checked content attribute, activation instead restores that author-provided default.

The use case is an optional form question where a user accidentally selects an answer and currently has no native way to return the group to its initial no-selection state. Radio groups already support no selection initially and through script; the proposal makes that state reachable through user activation.
